answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation contract: each identity locks scarce tokens, then gains weight gradually as independent peers attest to completed tasks and those attestations survive random audits. A falcon-like reviewer can challenge a claim; a proven lie burns the bond and slashes the endorsers’ stake. Spreading influence across many identities therefore requires capital for every bond and risks losing it, while the wharf of genuine work cannot be skipped by creating names on a ledge.
